competition: Belgian Mathematical Olympiad (Olympiade Mathématique Belge) - MAXI National Final

problems.problem:
Triangle $ABC$ is equilateral. The ray $BE$ meets segment $AC$ at $D$, with $\angle CBE=20^\circ$ and $DE=AB$. Find $\angle BEC$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/be_2007_p1_fig.png

Arrange $n$ digits $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$, each between $0$ and $9$, successively around a circle. Starting at $a_1$ and going around the circle forms the number $A_1=\overline{a_1a_2\cdots a_n}$. Starting at $a_2$ and going in the same direction forms $A_2=\overline{a_2a_3\cdots a_na_1}$, and so on. Is the proposition “if $d$ divides $A_1$, then $d$ also divides every $A_i$, $i\in\{2,3,\ldots,n\}$” true:

(a) for $d=9$?

(b) for $d=27$ and $n=2007$?

(c) for $d=27$ and every $n$?

Consider a set of $n$ points, no three collinear, and all triangles whose vertices belong to this set.

(a) If the points lie in a plane and $n=7$, what is the maximum number of these triangles that a line in this plane containing none of the seven points can intersect?

(b) If the points lie in space and $n=7$, what is the maximum number of these triangles that a plane containing none of the seven points can intersect?

(c) Generalise to arbitrary $n$.
Let $f$ be a function from the natural numbers to the natural numbers such that $f(n+1)>f(n)$ and $f(f(n))=3n$. Find $f(2007)$.

Let $r$ be the inradius, $R$ the circumradius, $p$ the perimeter and $c$ the hypotenuse of a right triangle.

(a) Prove that $\dfrac pc-\dfrac rR=2$.

(b) What is the greatest possible value of $r/R$ among all right triangles? For which right triangles is it attained?
Determine all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $f(x)\le x$ for every real $x$ and $f(x+y)\le f(x)+f(y)$ for all real $x,y$.

Let $r>0$ be real and let $n\ge3$ be an integer. There are $n$ points in the plane such that, among any three of them, at least two are at distance at most $r$. Prove that there are two disks of radius $r$ whose union contains all $n$ points.

Let $M$ and $N$ be points on the sides $[AB]$ and $[BC]$, respectively, of a rectangle $ABCD$. Let $a$ be the area of triangle $AMD$, $b$ that of triangle $MBN$ and $c$ that of triangle $NCD$. Express the area of triangle $DMN$ in terms of $a$, $b$ and $c$.
Determine all triples of natural numbers $(x,y,z)$ such that $$\frac{x}{7}+\frac{y}{11}+\frac{z}{13}=0.946053946053\ldots$$ (the right-hand side is a repeating decimal with period $6$).
Prove that there is no function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x$ and $y$, $$f\big(x+f(y^3)\big)=y+f(x^3).$$

Two circles $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $\mathcal{C}_2$ intersect at two distinct points $P$ and $Q$. Let $R$ be a point on $\mathcal{C}_1$ and $S$ a point on $\mathcal{C}_2$ such that $R$, $Q$ and $S$ are collinear. The lines $RP$ and $SP$ meet $\mathcal{C}_2$ and $\mathcal{C}_1$ again at $N$ and $M$, respectively. Let $T$ be the intersection of $RM$ and $SN$. Show that triangle $TMN$ is equilateral if and only if $MN$ is tangent to both circles.

(a) Determine all natural numbers that are multiples of $6$ and have exactly $6$ natural divisors.

(b) How many natural numbers are multiples of $2010$ and have exactly $2010$ natural divisors?

(a) Prove that if, in a triangle $ABC$, the angle at $A$ is twice the angle at $B$, then $$|BC|^2=|AC|^2+|AC|\cdot|AB|.$$

(b) Is the converse true?

(a) For which natural number(s) $n$ is $n^2+n+14$ the square of a natural number?

(b) For which natural number(s) $k$ does there exist at least one natural number $n$ for which $n^2+n+k$ is the square of a natural number?
In triangle $ABC$, let $H$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$. Let $E$ be the point where the bisector of the angle at $B$ meets side $AC$. Given that $\angle BEA=45^\circ$, determine $\angle EHC$.

(a) Determine all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that, for all real numbers $x$ and $y$, $$f(x+y)=2011^y\cdot f(x)+2012^x\cdot f(y).$$

(b) Determine all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that, for all real numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$, $$f(x+y+z)=2010^y\cdot f(x)+2011^z\cdot f(y)+2012^x\cdot f(z).$$

Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle. The points $K$, $L$, $M$ and $N$ are chosen on the open sides $]AB[$, $]BC[$, $]CD[$ and $]DA[$, respectively. The intersection point of $KM$ and $LN$ is denoted $P$.

(a) Do $KM\perp LN$ and $P\in BD$ imply $KL\parallel MN$?

(b) Do $P\in BD$ and $KL\parallel MN$ imply $KM\perp LN$?

(c) Do $KL\parallel MN$ and $KM\perp LN$ imply $P\in BD$?

Eleven contestants (Alexandre, Bérénice, $\ldots$, Knud) take part in a tournament in which they compete in bouts of five, in such a way that, at the end of the tournament, each contestant has faced each of his ten opponents exactly twice.

(a) In how many bouts does a contestant take part?

(b) How many bouts make up this tournament?

(c) Can it happen that three contestants were together in several bouts?

(d) Give an arrangement of the bouts of such a tournament.

Let $x$ be a real number.

(a) There exist three distinct integers $a$, $b$ and $c$ such that $a+x$, $b+x$ and $c+x$ are three consecutive terms of a geometric sequence; does this imply that the number $x$ is rational?

(b) If the number $x$ is rational, do there exist three distinct integers $a$, $b$ and $c$ such that $a+x$, $b+x$ and $c+x$ are three consecutive terms of a geometric sequence?

Consider a rectangular parallelepiped $ABCDEFGH$ (see the figure).

(a) If this parallelepiped is a cube, what is the measure of the angle $\angle FCH$?

(b) Can the edge lengths of this parallelepiped be chosen so that the angle $\angle FCH$ measures $45^\circ$?

(c) What are all the values that the measure of the angle $\angle FCH$ can take?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/be_2012_p1_fig.png

Consider the equation $pq+qr+pr+1=pqr$ in the unknowns $p$, $q$, $r$, which are prime numbers.

(a) Give one solution.

(b) Show that in each of its solutions, $p$, $q$ and $r$ are distinct.

(c) Give all its solutions.

A theatre has $20$ rows of $12$ seats each, the seats also forming $12$ columns. When they take their seats, the spectators always sit so as to form an interval in each row (that is, the seats of a row lying between two occupied seats are themselves all occupied). Once the spectators are seated, one counts for each column the number of occupied seats in it, which gives a list of $12$ natural numbers. The lists of $12$ natural numbers obtained in this way are called realizable.

(a) Is the list $(5,5,5,5,2,1,0,2,3,6,7,5)$ realizable? And the list $(1,2,8,1,7,4,1,6,1,1,4,1)$?

(b) Is every list of $12$ natural numbers all less than $5$ realizable?

(c) What is the largest natural number $k$ such that every list of $12$ natural numbers all between $0$ and $k$ is realizable?

(d) What is the smallest natural number $k$ such that every list of $12$ natural numbers all between $k$ and $20$ is realizable?

(e) Give a test (bearing only on the $12$ numbers $n_k$) that determines whether a list $(n_1,n_2,n_3,n_4,n_5,n_6,n_7,n_8,n_9,n_{10},n_{11},n_{12})$ is realizable or not.

An open disc (that is, without its boundary) of radius $1$ is divided into open regions by two lines.

(a) If the two lines are parallel, is there always an open disc of radius $1/3$ entirely contained in one of these regions?

(b) If the two lines are perpendicular, is there always an open disc of radius $1/3$ entirely contained in one of these regions?

(c) Is there always an open disc of radius $1/3$ entirely contained in one of these regions, whatever the position of the two lines?

Let $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$.

(a) If $a\neq b$ and the numbers $a-b$ and $a^2-b^2$ are rational, is the same true of $a+b$?

(b) If the numbers $a+b$ and $a^2+b^2$ are rational, is the same true of $a^3+b^3$? Of $a^4+b^4$?

(c) If the numbers $a^2+b^2$, $a^3+b^3$ and $a^4+b^4$ are rational, is the same true of $a+b$?

An urn contains $m$ mauve balls and $n$ black balls. The pair $(m,n)$ of natural numbers is called adequate when the number $d$ of pairs of balls of different colours in this urn is equal to the number $e$ of pairs of distinct balls of the same colour.

(a) Show that the pair $(10,15)$ is adequate.

(b) If $m=6$, what are all the adequate pairs $(6,n)$?

(c) How many adequate pairs $(m,n)$ are there? Describe their set.

Let $ABCD$ be a square of side $1$ and $A'B'C'D$ its image under a rotation $r$ with centre $D$. The intersection of these two squares is the quadrilateral $DALC'$. Through $C'$, the line parallel to $AD$ is drawn; it meets $AB$ at $E$ (see the figure).

(a) What is the area of the quadrilateral $DALC'$ if $E$ is the midpoint of $[AB]$?

(b) Determine the position of $E$ on $[AB]$ for which the area of $DALC'$ is half the area of the initial square.

(c) Determine the position of $E$ on $[AB]$ for which the area of $DALC'$ is $1/3$, $1/4$, $\ldots$, $1/m$ of the area of the initial square ($m$ being a nonzero natural number).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/be_2013_p3_fig.png

(a) Is there a multiple of $11$ whose digit sum is $6$?

(b) Is there a multiple of $11$ whose digit sum is $11$?

(c) Is there a multiple of $11$ whose digit sum is $3$?

(d) Find all natural numbers $n$ for which there exists a multiple of $11$ whose digit sum equals $n$.

The Babeleirs speak Babelanguage, which is written with an alphabet of two letters, $A$ and $B$. The words of their lexicon are all the words that result from the following rules, and only those:

R1. The one-letter word $B$ belongs to the lexicon.

R2. If a word of the lexicon contains a $B$, the word obtained by replacing this $B$ by $ABA$ also belongs to the lexicon.

R3. If a word of the lexicon contains two successive letters $A$, the word obtained by replacing them by a $B$ also belongs to the lexicon.

R4. If a word of the lexicon contains two successive letters $B$, the word obtained by deleting them also belongs to the lexicon.

(a) Does the word $AA$ belong to the lexicon of Babelanguage?

(b) Does the word $AAA$ belong to the lexicon?

(c) Does the empty word (consisting of zero letters) belong to the lexicon?

(d) Does the word $BABA$ belong to the lexicon?

(e) Describe the set of words of the lexicon containing exactly two letters $B$.

(f) How many words of $n$ letters are there in the lexicon of Babelanguage?

Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a sphere of radius $R$ tangent to a plane $\pi$. Eight other spheres, all of the same radius $r$, are tangent to $\pi$ and tangent to $\mathcal{S}$; they form a necklace in which each of them is tangent to its two neighbours. Express $r$ in terms of $R$.

Consider the following system of equations in the integer unknowns $x$ and $y$: $$\begin{cases}x^2+y=a\\ x+y^2=b\end{cases}$$ where $a$ and $b$ are two integer parameters.

(a) Show that the system has no solution if $a$ and $b$ have different parities.

(b) Find a pair $(a,b)$, with $a$ and $b$ distinct but of the same parity, for which the system has no solution.

(c) Show that the system has at most one solution for every pair $(a,b)$ with $a\neq b$.

A pencil number is a figurate number of the form shown in the figure (rows $1,\ldots,l$, columns $1,\ldots,k$). For example, the figure shows that $60=\mathrm{nc}(14,5)$. If $n$ is a nonzero natural number, a pencil writing of $n$ is a pair $(k,l)$ of natural numbers with $k\geqslant l\geqslant 1$ such that $n=\mathrm{nc}(k,l)$. Every nonzero natural number $n$ has at least one pencil writing, since $n=\mathrm{nc}(n,1)$.

(a) How many pencil writings do $2$, $8$ and $15$ have?

(b) How many pencil writings does $2014$ have?

(c) Express the number of pencil writings of a nonzero natural number in terms of its prime factorization.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/be_2014_p4_fig.png
Find all solutions of the system of equations $$\begin{cases}\sqrt{x^2-y}=z-1\\ \sqrt{y^2-z}=x-1\\ \sqrt{z^2-x}=y-1,\end{cases}$$ in the real unknowns $x$, $y$, $z$.

All non-empty words formed of pairwise different letters appearing in alphabetical order are arranged in the order determined by the following two rules:

• If the word $m_2$ contains a letter that comes, in the alphabet, after all the letters of the word $m_1$, then $m_1$ precedes $m_2$;

• If the words $m_1$ and $m_2$ are different but have the same last letter, two cases are distinguished: if moreover $m_1$ and $m_2$ each have at least two letters, then $m_1$ and $m_2$ are arranged in the same order as the words obtained by removing their last letter; if moreover one of the two words $m_1$ and $m_2$ consists of a single letter, then it comes before the other word.

The dictionary thus begins A, B, AB, C, AC, BC, ABC, D, AD, BD, $\ldots$ What rank does the word DEFI occupy in this dictionary?
Is the inequality $$x^3+y^3\leqslant x^3\sqrt[3]{\frac{x}{y}}+y^3\sqrt[3]{\frac{y}{x}}$$ true for all strictly positive real numbers $x$ and $y$?

In triangle $ABC$, the point $M$ is the midpoint of $[AB]$ and $D$ is the foot of the bisector of the angle $\angle ABC$. Moreover, $MD\perp BD$.

(a) Indicate how to construct such a triangle (with ruler and compass).

(b) Prove that $|AB|=3|BC|$.

(c) Is the condition $MD\perp BD$ necessary for $|AB|=3|BC|$?

A rectangular sheet of paper $ABCD$ of width $|AB|=4$ and length $|BC|=6$ is folded so that the lower right corner $B$ is brought onto a point $S$ of the left edge $[AD]$. The fold follows the segment $[RT]$, with $R$ on the lower edge $[AB]$ of the sheet and $T$ on its right edge $[BC]$. Let $x=|RB|$ and $y=|BT|$ (see the figure).

(a) What are the minimum and maximum values of $x$?

(b) Establish a relation between $x$ and $y$.

(c) Find the value of $x$ for which the area of the folded part (the triangle $RST$) is minimal. What is then the nature of the triangle $BST$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/be_2016_p1_fig.png
Solve the equation $2^{2m+1}+9\cdot 2^m+5=n^2$ in the integer unknowns $m$ and $n$.

In the plane, the triangles $ABD$ and $BCE$ lie outside the triangle $ABC$ and are right isosceles triangles with right angles at $D$ and at $C$, respectively. The point $H$ is the intersection of $CD$ and $AE$. Show that $BH$ and $AE$ are perpendicular.

A rectangular chocolate bar is divided into $mn$ squares by $m-1$ break lines parallel to its width and $n-1$ break lines parallel to its length.

(a) To end up with $mn$ small square pieces, I repeatedly break one of the pieces I have along what remains of one of the original break lines. How many breaks will I have to make at least? At most?

A dislocation of the chocolate bar is a list $\big([A_1B_1],[A_2B_2],\ldots,[A_kB_k]\big)$ of segments such that the breaks, made in this order along these segments, divide the bar into small squares. For example, for the $2\times 2$ bar in the figure, $\big([DF],[BE],[EH]\big)$ is a dislocation. Let $f(m,n)$ be the number of dislocations of an $m\times n$ bar.

(b) Show that $f(2,2)=4$.

(c) What is $f(2,3)$?

(d) Determine $f(2,n)$ in terms of $f(2,1)$, $f(2,2)$, $\ldots$, $f(2,n-1)$.

(e) For which values of $n$ is the natural number $f(2,n)$ divisible by $11$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/be_2016_p4_fig.png

At the start, seven dwarfs each have a glass containing a certain quantity of milk. This quantity may differ from glass to glass; some glasses may contain no milk, but the total quantity is not zero.

The first dwarf pours the whole content of his glass into the other glasses, sharing it out equally (and without loss). Then the second dwarf does the same with the new content of his glass, then the third, and so on, up to the seventh. The dwarfs then observe that each glass contains exactly the quantity it had at the start.

(a) At the start, which dwarf has the glass containing the least milk, and how much does it contain?

(b) Is it true that the quantities contained in the glasses at the start decrease from the first to the last dwarf?

(c) If the total quantity of milk is $21$ dL, are the starting quantities in the different glasses determined? What are all the possibilities?

The quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a semicircle of which $[AB]$ is a diameter; $|BC|=|CD|=a$, $|DA|=b\neq a$ and $|AB|=c$. If $a$, $b$, $c$ are natural numbers, show that $c$ cannot be a prime number.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/be_2017_p2_fig.png

Consider the sequence defined, for all $n$, by $$\begin{cases}t_0=1\\ t_{2n}=t_n\\ t_{2n+1}=1-t_n.\end{cases}$$

(a) What are the possible values of the terms of the sequence?

(b) Compute $t_{2017}$.

(c) Does the sequence contain $3$ equal consecutive terms?

(d) Express the value of $t_k$ in terms of the decomposition of $k$ as a sum of distinct powers of $2$.

(e) Is the sequence periodic?
In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, the angles at $B$ and at $C$ are greater than $120^\circ$. Show that $|AC|+|BD|>|AB|+|BC|+|CD|$.

The real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ and $e$ are unknown to me at present, but I know two things: first their order $a\leqslant b\leqslant c\leqslant d\leqslant e$, and then the results, in no particular order, of the ten sums of these numbers taken two at a time. Does this information allow me to find:

(a) the sum $a+b+c+d+e$?

(b) the value of $c$?

(c) the value of each of the numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $e$?
Let $a$ and $b$ be two real numbers such that $\left(a+\sqrt{1+a^2}\right)\left(b+\sqrt{1+b^2}\right)=1$. What is $(a+b)^{2018}$?

In the acute triangle $ABC$, $|AB|\neq|AC|$. The points $P$ and $Q$ are the feet of the altitudes from $B$ and from $C$, respectively. The line $PQ$ meets the line $BC$ at $R$. Show that the bisectors of the angles $\angle BAC$ and $\angle PRB$ are perpendicular.

The integers from $0$ to $2018$ are written on the board. A student chooses any two of them, erases them and replaces them by a single number equal to:

• their sum, if both are even;

• the opposite of their sum, if both are odd;

• the odd number minus the even number, if they have different parities.

The operation is repeated until only one number remains on the board.

(a) Give an example of a final result that can be obtained.

(b) How many different results can be obtained, depending on the order in which the numbers are taken? What are these results?
The polynomial $P(x)=x^3-2x^2-3x+1$ has three real roots $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$. What is $\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3$?

The triangle $ABC$ has three acute angles. Its altitudes $[AD]$, $[BE]$ and $[CF]$ are extended to meet the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at $X$, $Y$ and $Z$, respectively. What is the value of $$\frac{|AX|}{|AD|}+\frac{|BY|}{|BE|}+\frac{|CZ|}{|CF|}:$$

(a) if the triangle $ABC$ is equilateral?

(b) if the triangle $ABC$ is an arbitrary acute triangle?

A $9\times 9$ square is divided into $81$ cells of size $1\times 1$.

(a) What is the largest number of cells such that no two of these cells are ever in the same row or in the same column?

(b) What is the largest number of cells such that no two of these cells ever touch at exactly one corner?

(c) What is the largest number of cells such that no two of these cells are ever on the same line parallel to one of the two diagonals?

(d) What is the largest number of cells such that any two of these cells always have their centres at a distance different from $\sqrt{5}$?

(a) For which natural numbers $n$ is the number $n^4-20n^2+75$ a prime natural number?

(b) For which natural numbers $n$ is the number $n^4-3n^2+9$ a prime natural number?

A supermarket displays chocolate by stacking boxes in a construction with $p$ levels. Each level is rectangular in shape and has one box fewer than the level below it, both in length and in width.

(a) If the last level (the top level), of rank $p$, consists of $m$ rows of $n$ boxes each, express the total number $S$ of boxes of the construction in terms of $m$, $n$ and $p$, in the most simplified form possible.

(b) What is the largest possible value of $S$ if $mn=6$ and $p=10$?

An examination session is organised for the sixth year at the Institut Saint-Eddy-Merckx. On the first day, the $E$ sixth-year students sit an exam. They are distributed among $L$ rooms, with $L$ nonzero; each room contains a different number of students, at least three. Unfortunately, cheaters are detected. They are excluded from the second exam, which all the other students sit on the following day. This second exam is organised in some nonzero number of rooms; once again, each room contains a different number of students, at least three. Moreover, the organisers manage to satisfy the following condition: two students who sat the first exam in the same room never sit the second exam in the same room as each other.

(a) If $E=12$ and $L=3$, the conditions above determine the number of cheaters detected; how many are there?

(b) In the general case, show that at least $2L+3$ cheaters are detected.

(c) Under what condition(s) on $E$ and $L$ is it possible that exactly $2L+3$ cheaters are detected?

The circle $\mathcal{C}$ with centre $I$ and radius $r$ is inscribed in the triangle $ABC$. The sides $[BC]$, $[AC]$ and $[AB]$ have lengths $a$, $b$, $c$, respectively, and are tangent to $\mathcal{C}$ at the points $X$, $Y$ and $Z$. What is the norm of the vector $a\overrightarrow{IX}+b\overrightarrow{IY}+c\overrightarrow{IZ}$?

For a positive integer $a$, define $a!=a(a-1)\cdots1$.

(a) Is there an integer $a$ with $2\le a\le100$ such that $a!$ is a perfect square? If so, which one?

(b) Is $P=1!\cdot2!\cdot3!\cdots100!$ a perfect square?

(c) Is there an integer $a$ with $1\le a\le100$ such that $P/a!$ is a perfect square? If so, find all possible $a$. If not, do there exist distinct integers $a,b$ between $1$ and $100$ such that $P/(a!b!)$ is a perfect square?

A rhombus $AECF$ of side length $1$ is constructed around a square $ABCD$ of side length $x$, where $0<x<1$, as shown.

(a) Express in terms of $x$ the area of the shaded region, inside the rhombus and outside the square.

(b) For which $x$ is this shaded area maximal?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/belgium_2022_p2_fig.png

Three shaded squares are constructed externally on the sides of triangle $ABC$. Three unshaded squares are constructed using vertices of the shaded squares, as shown.

(a) If $ABC$ is a right triangle, what is the ratio of the sum of the areas of the unshaded squares to the sum of the areas of the shaded squares?

(b) What is this ratio for an arbitrary triangle?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/belgium_2022_p3_fig.png

A school has $590$ pupils, to be divided into $25$ classes, each containing between $18$ and $28$ pupils.

(a) Can the pupils be divided so that $22$ classes have the same size?

(b) Find the largest integer $n$ for which some division has $n$ classes of the same size.

(c) Can the pupils be divided so that no three classes have the same size?

(d) Find the largest integer $n$ such that every division has at least $n$ classes of the same size.

The notation $\overline{a_k\cdots a_2a_1a_0}_b$ denotes the number whose base-$b$ digits are $a_k,\ldots,a_2,a_1,a_0$. For example, $\overline{235}_{10}=2\cdot10^2+3\cdot10+5=235$, while $\overline{235}_7=2\cdot7^2+3\cdot7+5=124$. Find all triples $(x,y,z)$ with $x,y,z\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ and $x\ne0$ such that $$\overline{xyz}_{10}=2\overline{xyz}_7.$$

Two identical rectangular pieces of card, of length $a$ and width $b$, with $a>b$, are placed side by side as in the left figure. The left card is rotated about its bottom right corner $P$ until its top right corner reaches the right edge of the right card, as in the right figure.

(a) Prove that the top left corner of the right card then also touches the left edge of the left card.

(b) Express the area of the shaded overlap in terms of $a,b$.

(c) If $a,b$ and the area of the overlap are integers, what is the smallest possible length $a$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/belgium_2023_p2_fig.png
Find all real triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $$\begin{cases}x+y+\frac1z=3,\\x+\frac1y+z=3,\\\frac1x+y+z=3.\end{cases}$$
Three spheres are pairwise tangent and tangent to the same plane. Their points of contact with the plane form a triangle of side lengths $3,6,4$. What are the radii of the spheres?

Johan leaves $X$ at sunrise and walks at constant speed, reaching $Y$ at $16{:}00$. Pirlouit leaves $Y$ at sunrise and walks at constant speed along the same path in the opposite direction, reaching $X$ at $21{:}00$. They meet at noon. At what time was sunrise?

Is the difference between the cube of a sum of integers and the sum of their cubes always divisible by $3$:

(a) for a sum of two integers?

(b) for a sum of three integers?

(c) for a sum of $n$ integers?
Points $B,C,D,E$ lie on a line in that order. Triangle $ABE$ is right-angled at $B$, and $\angle BAC=\angle CAD=\angle DAE$. Express $DE$ as simply as possible in terms of $a=BC$ and $b=CD$.

Let $S(n)$ be the sum of the decimal digits of a nonnegative integer $n$. A trunk of $n$ is a number obtained by deleting one or more of its rightmost digits. For example, the trunks of $2345$ are $234,23,2$. Let $T(n)$ be the sum of all the trunks of $n$. Prove that $$\frac{n-S(n)}{T(n)}$$ is an integer independent of $n$ for every integer $n\ge10$.
For which decimal digits $x,y$ is the number $\overline{30x0y03}$ a multiple of $13$? Find all pairs $(x,y)$.

All pupils in a class have distinct heights. Their teacher wants to arrange them in a line in which the heights first increase and then decrease. Entirely increasing and entirely decreasing lines are also allowed. How many such lines are there when the number of pupils is:

(a) $3$?

(b) $4$?

(c) an arbitrary positive integer $n$?
Find all integer pairs $(x,y)$ such that $$x+y=x^2-xy+y^2.$$

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Let $B\prime$ and $C\prime$ be the reflections of $B$ and $C$ in the lines $AC$ and $AB$, respectively. Let $P\ne A$ be the intersection of the circumcircles of triangles $ABB\prime$ and $ACC\prime$. Prove that the circumcentre of triangle $ABC$ lies on the line $AP$.

Initially $10$ and $13$ are written on a board. Each minute, one new number appears: it is the sum of two distinct numbers already on the board, and it has not appeared before. Thus no number occurs twice.

(a) Can the process be carried out so that $2026$ eventually appears?

(b) Can it be carried out so that $68$ eventually appears?

(c) Can it be carried out so that $95$ eventually appears? If so, after how many minutes at the earliest?
Let $p$ and $s$ be the product and sum, respectively, of three primes $a,b,c$. One of $p,s$ equals $101$ times the other. Determine $a,b,c$.

Twenty-seven balls are numbered from $1$ to $27$. Of these, $r$ are red, $b$ are blue and $j$ are yellow, with no other colours. The arithmetic means of the numbers on the red, blue and yellow balls are $15,3,18$, respectively. Find all triples $(r,b,j)$ for which this is possible.

Let $E$ be the midpoint of $AB$ in square $ABCD$. Point $F$ is inside the square and satisfies $\angle CFE=\angle BCF=\angle CDF=\alpha$, as shown.

(a) If $H,I$ are the midpoints of $CD,CF$, respectively, prove that the lines $BC,EF,HI$ are concurrent.

(b) Determine $\alpha$.
